messages:
Marta: Heads up — we're seeing steady tail latency and occasional OOM-ish failures from a dedicated pool in us-east-1 starting ~10:12 UTC. Not typical thermal pattern.
Ryan: Which pool id?
Marta: pool-dedicated-23 (eu/edge style naming but mapped to us-east-1). Latency spikes correlate with a sharp rise in NIC tx_queue length on the host.
Anika: Can you paste the grafana query that shows the correlation?
Marta: sure:
```
sum(rate(nic_tx_queue_length[1m])) by (host) / sum(nvidia_gpu_utilization) by (host)
```
Marta: spike at ~10:12 -> nic queue up, gpu util ok, but API token generation tails up and we started seeing allocator evictions.
Ops-Bot: Alert: pool-dedicated-23 egress-pressure HIGH (10:12 UTC). Auto-evac triggered for 2 pods.
Samir: Could be a noisy neighbor doing large pretrained-model uploads or grpc chat workloads over the same NIC. Any large uploads around that time?
Marta: we checked s3 ingress logs: one tenant did large checkpoint fetches (multi-gb) to warm ephemeral cache at 10:11.
Ryan: Hmm. That's a classic NIC vs HBM contention pattern on these backplane configs. We should confirm pcap or `ethtool -S` counters for drops.
Anika: I can spin a quick probe in the pool: run iperf for tx, and attach eBPF qdisc histograms. Give me 10m.
Ling: We should consider tagging that tenant with soft-egress QoS so it doesn't trample dedicated pool traffic. Can we hotfix by routing the tenant to a burst lane or separate egress shard?
Samir: Short-term: reroute the tenant to the shared-burst pool and add a rate limit on the manager side. Long-term: add NIC-aware placement to allocator so large downloads avoid low-egress hosts.
Ryan: FYI, the hardware here has a single 100G uplink per rack; when a host does multi-gb downloads it starves the host's local kernel queues and interrupts which the GPU stack depends on. We can try enabling irqbalance tweaks or limit the TCP tx queue via tc.
Marta: Trying a quick mitigation: set `tc qdisc tbf dev eth0 rate 4gbit burst 32k latency 50ms` on the host and see if latency eases.
Anika: Also running eBPF snapshot now, pushing to #eng-infra/artifacts.
Ops-Bot: Deploy job: apply-tc-mitigation started by Marta on host gpu-host-23. ID: jb-9843.
Ryan: If tc helps, we make a transient policy for dedicated pools to reserve an egress share. But need to weigh cost of carving dedicated egress vs. routing complexity.
Ling: For Dedicated customers we promised isolation — egress carveouts might be part of SLA. We should raise with product.
Samir: Cost note: reserving egress per pool will increase cross-AZ transit and provisioning overhead. Estimate needed before proposing.
Marta: Update: after tc push tail latency dropped ~40% in 4m window, eviction rate stopped.
Anika: Confirming from eBPF: kernel txq drain now stable, interrupts subsided. Nice.
Ryan: Follow-ups: 1) add NIC queue metrics to preflight for placement, 2) add tenant prewarm detection to throttle large checkpoint downloads, 3) design egress-share policy for Dedicated.
Ling: I'll open a short RFC for egress carveout options and SLA implications.
Samir: I'll sketch cost model — incremental bandwidth reservation vs. reactive routing cost.
Marta: Filing incident postmortem, attaching logs and the tc command we used. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Ryan: Great quick mitigation. Let's track if this recurs or if other pools show similar patterns.
Anika: note: we should also consider adding a small background process to detect long-lived high-throughput flows and signal allocator not to pack latency-sensitive tenants on same host.
Marta: Agreed. End of thread.
